key_insight: COSMA co-optimizes mapping, scheduling, and qubit allocation to cut inter-core communication for fermionic simulation on modular quantum computers.
engineering_relevance: It targets a key bottleneck in scalable quantum hardware, making multi-core quantum simulation more practical for chemistry and other fermionic workloads.
method: Pauli term scheduling to reduce transfers
Qubit allocation aware of inter-core communication cost
evidence_signal: On molecular benchmarks, COSMA reduces communication cost by up to 2.5× versus state-of-the-art baselines, with a median improvement of 1.7×.
watch_item: The gains depend on benchmark structure and modular hardware assumptions, so performance may vary on different circuits or interconnect topologies.
paper_title: COSMA: Communication-aware Optimization of Fermionic Simulation Kernels for Modular Quantum Architectures
